title: Command and an arrow key nudge a picked clip a frame in time
goal: Lining a clip up to a beat or a word is a frame-by-frame job. Premiere editors nudge a picked clip one frame earlier or later from the keyboard, five with Shift. Here the arrow keys always move the playhead, so the only way to shift a clip by one frame is a careful drag at high zoom.
notes: Keys table: Sources/PhotonzCore/TimelineKeys.swift (arrows at ~179-182 step frames only); handlers Sources/Photonz/EditorState+TimelineKeys.swift; menu rows Sources/Photonz/EditorCommands.swift (Option Shift arrows at ~995-1000 are caption timing; no Command arrow binding exists today, grep checked). Premiere's Nudge Clip Selection Left/Right: check its default Mac keyboard map before binding (recalled as Command Left/Right, Shift Command for five frames); if Premiere's Mac keys differ and are free here, use Premiere's. Reuse the move rule moveClips(byMS:) and the frame length from the document's frame rate. Found by the 2026-10-05 22:xx manager pass's key audit: no time-nudge function exists anywhere.
acceptance: With one or more clips picked on the timeline, Command Left and Command Right move them one frame earlier or later, Shift Command five frames, each press one undo step; with nothing picked the keys do nothing
A nudge that would run into the clip next to it on the same track, or before the start, stops at the edge rather than overlapping; a clip on a locked track does not move
The Clip menu (or wherever the clip's other time commands live in the menu bar) carries Nudge Earlier and Nudge Later with those keys, dimmed with nothing picked
Plain arrows still step the playhead; Option Shift arrows still move captions; Command arrows in a text field still move the caret

Try it at Next defaults: open a recording, cut it with Command K, click the second piece, press Command Right three times and read its start in the panel. A walk does the same and reads the start before and after. Audit written under queue/audits/; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: Before building: Premiere's Mac map has Nudge Clip Selection Left/Right on Cmd+Left/Right, Shift+Cmd for five; both were free here (only Option+Shift arrows, captions, were taken). Problem found: Cmd+K makes PIECES of one clip, not two clips, so a picked piece cannot move on its own without a gap the model has no way to hold. Decided: a nudge moves the whole clip, matching a Cmd drag on a piece. Asked in the audit's evaluate list rather than on a decision card, since the user's reaction to that line becomes a task.

Second danger: a menu key equivalent fires before a text field gets the key. Fixed: the menu rows print their keys only while the timeline has the keyboard (same as J/K/L), and when a field has the keyboard the row hands the caret move to the field, the way Cut/Copy/Paste do. The walk proves it: renaming a clip, Cmd+Left reached the Clip menu row, which moved the caret to the front, and the clip did not move.

Built: PhotonzCore/ClipNudge.swift (canNudgeClips, nudgeClips(byFrames:) stop at the clip next door on the same track and at 0; locked-track clips stay; tests ClipNudgeTests, 13). TimelineKeys .nudgeClips(frames:) on Cmd/Shift+Cmd arrows, timeline focus only (TimelineKeysTests). App: EditorState+ClipNudge.swift (Next only via the cutRecording flag), Clip menu rows Nudge Earlier/Later (EditorCommands nudgeClipRows). Walk command-arrows-nudge-a-clip-walk (front:true, needs the Mac: windowClick plus menus) green; neighbouring walks premiere-keys, every-command-in-the-menu-bar, a-click-on-a-clip-piece green; Scripts/test.sh 11464 passed.

Rough items: the piece-vs-whole-clip question is in the audit's evaluate list for the user to answer. The missing menu rows for the five-frame nudge and the fixed 33ms frame are left rough here: a person barely notices either and neither clears the follow-up bar.
